audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven chart rows contradict both the packet chart and the page's own prose. Page reads Nautilus / Skill / Morde / Morde / Morde / Morde / Morde; packet reads Skill / Morde / Morde / Skill / Skill / Morde / Nautilus.
audit.why: whys[0] says levels 1-2 are an even standoff, whys[1] says your Q+W out-trade him, whys[3] says his root and slow 'cancel out to even', whys[4] says the lane 'stalls into an even shove-and-poke duel', whys[6] says 'Full-tank Naut reclaims it'. The prose already matches the packet, not the sides.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 3, 4 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as one atomic group -> Skill, Mordekaiser, (3 unchanged), Skill, Skill, (5 unchanged), Nautilus. Ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as a Mordekaiser spike; it is not one here.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140/120/100s at 650 range and isolates a target you cannot kill — Nautilus is a tank with Titan's Wrath (12s shield). The real Morde spikes are level 3 and the first magic-damage item; Nautilus's is two items of tank stats.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten as a hold-your-R row; the 2+ item row given to Nautilus.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers on Dredge Line or Riptide, and the terrain use of Dredge Line was never stated.
audit.why: Dredge Line: 1150 range, 14/13/12/11/10s, knockup + hard CC, and colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it — so he can cut off your retreat, and Mordekaiser has no dash. Riptide: 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s, 600 range, three slowing waves — the tool that drags you out of Darkness Rise range. Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against a target.
audit.corrected: Track Dredge Line's 14s and commit inside it; hold Flash for the terrain hook, not for damage; reset before Staggering Blow comes back up.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were copy-pasted boilerplate that did not match their own titles ('Eat his passive root chain', 'R into his W shield').
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a 12s shield that adds damage over time to his attacks — the actual reason not to dump the Realm into him.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to their titles.

edits.before: Q start, but it's slow and telegraphed — Nautilus dodges it on reaction at full HP. Last-hit, aim isolated Qs only when he commits to a CS.
edits.after: Q start, but it's slow — Nautilus sidesteps it at full HP and answers from 1150 range. Last-hit, and Q only when he steps up for a CS.

edits.before: Q ranks make isolated hits massive. Nautilus must hug minions all lane; punish every step away from the wave with the full drag combo.
edits.after: Q ranks make isolated hits massive, but Staggering Blow's root and Riptide's slow chip you out of aura range — it cancels out to even.

edits.before: Realm of Death online — the 1v1 Nautilus cannot decline. R steals 10% of his stats; take the duel whenever Dredge Line (Hook) is down and the wave is shoved.
edits.after: Realm of Death is 140s at rank 1 and low value on a tank you cannot kill 1v1 — hold it for his carry and treat the lane as an even shove-and-poke duel.

edits.before: Riftmaker omnivamp turns the Realm 1v1 unloseable into most matchups. Nautilus's only outs are dodging Q forever or never being alone — neither survives a whole game.
edits.after: Full-tank Nautilus reclaims it: Dredge Line into a Staggering Blow root into Depth Charge chain-locks you while he tanks Darkness Rise for his team to collapse.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Nautilus Dredge Line: Hurls an anchor; on a champ hit, pulls both together — his hook. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Q): matchup-defining — a 1150-range hook on 14s at rank 1. Dodge it, then commit inside that window. - Nautilus Riptide (E): 7s, three slowing waves — the chip that pulls you out of Darkness Rise.

edits.before: His only engage. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1. Dodge it, then commit in that window.

edits.before: That is Nautilus's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: You have no dash — hold Flash for the hook that cuts your retreat, not for damage.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack against you — reset before it is back.

edits.before: Whiffing Q into the wave and trading with no passive stacks — un-isolated Obliterate hits soft, and without Darkness Rise you lose most even exchanges.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath shields him and his autos burn damage over time — a Realm on a tank you cannot kill just spends 140s of your best cooldown for nothing.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'His Staggering Blow' in whys[3] — FALSE POSITIVE, Staggering Blow is Nautilus's real passive. The genuine defect was the level chart: five of seven rows disagreed with the packet chart AND with the page's own whys/spikes prose, which already describes 1-2 as even, 4-5 and 6 as even, and 2+ items as Nautilus's. All five rows are proposed as one atomic paired group (full phases[N].side + content win[N] together) with matching rating moves. Not asserted (kits do not cover it): whether Depth Charge's knockup is reduced by tenacity, and whether Dredge Line can interrupt Realm of Death's cast.
